clue.text: Situation resolved by changing one's locks?

definitions.text: Situation resolved by changing one's locks?

parts.words: Situation resolved by changing one's locks?
parts.note: surface reading: a security problem fixed by fitting new door locks
setter's reading: locks are strands of hair, so the trouble is an unruly hairstyle fixed by a new look

explanation.walkthrough: Locks suggests a burglary and a locksmith; read it as hair and the situation is a day when your hair will not behave.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a day when one's hairstyle looks wrong, figuratively any day where everything goes badly.

clue.text: Seen here: Normans having Saxons in stitches?

definitions.text: Seen here: Normans having Saxons in stitches?

parts.note: surface reading: the invaders keeping the English laughing helplessly
setter's reading: a place where the famous embroidery of the Norman Conquest, sewn in stitches, is on display

explanation.walkthrough: In stitches usually means laughing; here it is literal embroidery, the tapestry depicting the Norman invasion of England in 1066, kept in a Normandy town.
explanation.definitionFit: The Normandy town houses the celebrated embroidered tapestry that shows the conquest, so that is where the stitched Saxons are seen.

clue.text: Stupid wife wearing glove stopped working outside

indicators.note: something worn is enclosed by clothing, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a machine that stopped working has died

indicators.note: being on the outside means wrapping around the remaining letters

parts.note: a mitt is a glove
W is the standard abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A daft wife sits in her mitten while something breaks down around her.
explanation.walkthrough: The wife goes inside the glove after its first letter, then the whole lot is wrapped by the verb for stopped working.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adjectives describing someone slow on the uptake, lacking intelligence or sense; a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Article, canny one, excited anger

parts.note: the indefinite article

indicators.note: excited things are stirred up and agitated, so these letters are thrown about

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece by a shrewd writer stirs up readers' fury.
explanation.walkthrough: Canny is Scottish and northern English for shrewd or careful, which suits the surface but is just fodder here.
explanation.definitionFit: Annoyance is a mild form of irritation, and anger here is a noun for that same displeased feeling.

clue.text: Recall a leading Russian religious adherent

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the letters run back the other way

parts.note: taken as written
the tsar was Russia's ruler, its leading figure

explanation.surface: Remembering a prominent Russian who followed a particular faith.
explanation.walkthrough: Leading Russian is a single idea, the old title of Russia's emperor, not a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rasta is a follower of Rastafarianism, the Jamaican religious movement, so a believer in that faith.

clue.text: Approve including role: act ultimately flat

indicators.note: to include something is to take it inside, so one piece is enclosed

parts.note: saying amen expresses approval or assent
an actor's role is a part

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the final letter is wanted

parts.note: the final letter of act

explanation.surface: Endorsing an actor's part, though the performance ends up lacking spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: Flat looks like a verdict on the acting, but it is the definition; the role sits inside the word of approval, and the last letter of act follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat is the British word for a set of rooms on one floor, which Americans call an apartment.

clue.text: Length taken from wood for bow

indicators.note: something taken from a whole is removed, leaving the rest behind

parts.note: larch is a timber tree
L is the abbreviation for length

explanation.surface: Cutting a length of timber to make an archer's bow.
explanation.walkthrough: Wood here is a type of tree, not raw material; the tree loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A bow is a curved shape, and an arch is likewise a curved structure or bend, as in to bow or arch the back.

clue.text: Stuns in dresses, not feminine

indicators.note: not means without, so that letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: frocks are dresses
F is the grammatical abbreviation for feminine

explanation.surface: Someone looks stunning in their gowns, though not in a girly way.
explanation.walkthrough: In dresses reads as a fashion compliment; in is just a link and dresses is the source word.
explanation.definitionFit: To rock someone is to shock or shake them badly, so a piece of news that rocks you stuns you.

clue.text: See 18
Finish second and first

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
being first is being top

explanation.surface: A race result: crossing the line second, and also first.
explanation.walkthrough: Finish second sounds like a placing in a race, but finish is the definition and second and first are the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To finish doing something is to cease or halt it, which is a plain verb synonym.

clue.text: Arabs here, missing start, watch team

indicators.note: missing its start means losing its opening letter

parts.note: to watch is to eye
a team is made up of its men

explanation.surface: Arab spectators watching a sports side that got off to a poor start.
explanation.walkthrough: Missing start applies to the verb watch only, which loses its first letter before the team is added.
explanation.definitionFit: The country lies on the southern Arabian peninsula, so it is a place where Arab people live.

clue.text: Gladiator to practise fighting distributed scuta

parts.note: to spar is to practise boxing or fighting

indicators.note: things distributed are spread around, so these letters are dealt out in a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A gladiator handing out Roman shields so the trainees can practise fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: Scuta is the Latin plural of scutum, the Roman legionary's shield, which makes the arena picture convincing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Thracian slave who led a revolt against Rome was trained and fought as a gladiator at Capua.

clue.text: Number one college extremely trendy

parts.note: uni is short for university, a college

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, so only the outer letters are wanted

parts.note: the first and last letters of trendy

explanation.surface: The top-ranked university is also extremely fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: Number one college reads as a league table; number one is the definition, and college is the piece.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics unity is another name for the numeral one, the multiplicative identity.

clue.text: Ace new wine with list introduced for starters

indicators.note: something introduced is brought in, so it is inserted among the other letters

parts.note: Asti is an Italian sparkling wine
N is the abbreviation for new
to list is to lean, as does a ship, which is to tip
A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

explanation.surface: A splendid new wine arrives with a menu brought in for the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: List is not a menu but the verb to lean; it goes in between the opening pieces and the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasti are the Italian appetisers served before the main meal, so they are starters on a menu.

clue.text: Character restricting badger's weight

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: the tone of a place is its character
to badger someone is to nag them

explanation.surface: A wildlife figure keeping a badger on a diet to control its weight.
explanation.walkthrough: Badger is the verb meaning to pester, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonnage is a ship's capacity or total load measured in tons, so it is a measure of weight.

clue.text: Judge computing speed following a run

indicators.note: one thing following another comes after it, so the earlier-named piece is placed second

parts.note: taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
bit rate is the speed of data transfer in computing

explanation.surface: A judge measures how fast the computer goes after a jog.
explanation.walkthrough: Bit rate is the computing term for data speed, measured in bits per second.
explanation.definitionFit: To arbitrate is to settle a dispute as an impartial referee, so to judge between parties.

clue.text: Informal talk succeeded with Metropolis director

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees
Fritz Lang directed the 1927 silent film Metropolis

explanation.surface: A casual chat went well with the director of a classic science-fiction film.
explanation.walkthrough: Succeeded looks like a verb about the chat going well; it is the genealogical abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang is colloquial vocabulary used in casual speech rather than formal writing.

clue.text: Show place set out around clubs

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece wraps the other
things set out are laid out afresh, so these letters are arranged anew

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
C is the card abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A venue for a show laid out around nightclubs.
explanation.walkthrough: Place set looks like a dining-table phrase; set is part of the fodder, and out tells you to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectacle is a visually striking display or performance, so a show in the theatrical sense.

clue.text: Old country's bottomless pit in one area

parts.note: an abyss is a seemingly bottomless chasm
taken as written
the Roman numeral for one
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A former nation has a bottomless pit within a single region.
explanation.walkthrough: In reads like a container signal but is simply its own two letters in the chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Abyssinia is the historical name for Ethiopia, so it is a country under an old, superseded name.

clue.text: Fight notable as leaders of the Saxons scattered

definitions.text: Fight notable as leaders of the Saxons scattered

indicators.note: scattered things are strewn in disorder, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: leaders are those at the front, so only initial letters are taken

parts.note: the first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A famous battle in which the English side, without its commanders, broke and fled.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition word Fight is also part of the fodder, so the whole clue both builds and describes the answer, an &lit.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1066 clash was a notable fight in which King Harold fell and the Saxon army was routed by the Normans.

clue.text: Two daughters into the beer become confused

indicators.note: going into something means being placed inside it

parts.note: ale is beer
D is the abbreviation for daughter, so two of them

explanation.surface: Two girls get stuck into the beer and end up muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a verb phrase, and the answer works intransitively: eggs and brains can addle.
explanation.definitionFit: To addle, used intransitively, is to grow muddled, as an egg that goes off or a mind that loses clarity.

clue.text: What might be flat — as a pancake?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a power cell, which goes flat when drained

definitions.note: a phrase standing for an adjective; fair because the answer is read as batter plus Y, meaning batter-like, which describes a pancake
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a whimsical adjective for something like the mixture pancakes are made from

explanation.walkthrough: Flat as a pancake is a stock phrase, and the dash breaks it in two; the second half invents an adjective, batter plus Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A drained power cell is described as flat, and pancakes are cooked from a runny mix of flour, egg and milk.

clue.text: King's a king in control

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it

parts.note: to have hold over something is to control it
taken as written
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch is a king who holds power.
explanation.walkthrough: King appears twice: the first is the definition, the second is the single letter for rex.
explanation.definitionFit: Harold Godwinson was the English king killed at the 1066 battle, so the name belongs to a monarch.

clue.text: Okay to take to Dart eel that wriggles

indicators.note: a wriggling thing twists and squirms, so these letters writhe into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Fine to bring a squirming eel along to the river Dart.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dart is a river in Devon, south-west England, which makes the fishing picture; it is only fodder here.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tolerated is allowed or accepted, if grudgingly, so it is deemed acceptable, which is what okay means.

clue.text: Stars penning ultimately erotic material

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, as livestock in a fold, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: Lyra is a constellation, a group of stars

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so the final letter is wanted

parts.note: the final letter of erotic

explanation.surface: Celebrities writing racy content.
explanation.walkthrough: Penning suggests writing; it means enclosing, and material is fabric rather than written content.
explanation.definitionFit: Lycra is a trademarked stretchy synthetic fibre used for sportswear, so a kind of fabric or cloth.

clue.text: Power lacking in very quick incursion

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so that letter is removed

parts.note: rapid means very quick
P is the abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A lightning military strike carried out without enough force.
explanation.walkthrough: Very quick is one adjective to find before the single letter for power is taken out.
explanation.definitionFit: A raid is a sudden attack into enemy territory, just as an incursion is a hostile invasion.

clue.text: Old wit sent up harsh lawmaker

indicators.note: in a down entry sending something up makes it read from bottom to top

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
a card is a witty, amusing person

explanation.surface: A comedian of old mocked a severe legislator.
explanation.walkthrough: Sent up sounds like satire, but in a down clue it turns the letters upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Draco was the Athenian legislator whose severe code gave us the word draconian, so a famously strict law-giver.

clue.text: Inventive sort decorates Lancastrian houses

indicators.note: to house something is to give it a home inside, so the letters lie within the phrase

parts.note: the letters run across the boundary between these two words

explanation.surface: A creative person paints and decorates homes in Lancashire.
explanation.walkthrough: Houses reads as a noun for buildings; it is the verb meaning contains. A Lancastrian is someone from Lancashire in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Nikola Tesla was the inventor of alternating-current systems, so the surname names a famously inventive person.

clue.text: Deal with China involved food from elsewhere

indicators.note: something involved is intricate and tangled, so these letters are mixed together

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A trade agreement with Beijing covered imported foodstuffs.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the food is Chinese, but the letters of the two named words make a Mexican dish.
explanation.definitionFit: An enchilada is a filled, rolled tortilla from Mexico, so to a British solver it is a foreign dish.

clue.text: Worker in firm's poetry

indicators.note: being in something means being placed inside it

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: An employee writes verse for the company.
explanation.walkthrough: Worker is the crossword's favourite insect, the worker ant.
explanation.definitionFit: A canto is one of the major divisions of a long poem, as in Dante, so it is a section of verse.

clue.text: Great to cover large rolls of flesh

indicators.note: covering something means going all around it, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: fab is slang for great, short for fabulous
L is the clothing abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A large size is good for hiding bulges of fat.
explanation.walkthrough: Rolls hints at bread, but it means folds of body fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Flab is loose, excess body fat, which tends to hang in folds and bulges around the waist.

clue.text: Action at Wimbledon on live, or earlier

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the first piece follows the second here

parts.note: to live is to be, to exist
a forehand is a tennis stroke, and Wimbledon hosts the famous tennis championships

explanation.surface: A tennis match at Wimbledon broadcast live or recorded in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: Live sounds like broadcasting; it is the verb meaning to exist.
explanation.definitionFit: Beforehand means in advance or at an earlier time, so the two adverbs are interchangeable synonyms.
